head_commit.message:
fix(ops): read millisecond clocks from EPOCHREALTIME

Ubuntu 26.04 ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0, whose date ignores the %3N
width and prints unpadded nanoseconds (0.7.0 behaves the same; 0.9.0
fixed it). The gateway health probe on such a host published
multi-million latency_ms values and nanosecond request deadlines.

Replace the duplicated epoch-millis.sh helper with the bash builtin
EPOCHREALTIME, so neither the launcher nor the OPS bundle needs a
shared file or a date subprocess. The health probe test now runs the
real probe under a uutils-0.7-style date and fails on the old code.
